research_question: What is the effect of autoinflation compared with watchful waiting or no treatment on the persistence of otitis media with effusion (OME) in children at up to 6 weeks of follow-up?
outcome_description: Persistence of middle ear effusion at up to 6 weeks follow-up (closest to 4 weeks within the 2 to 6 week window), defined as a flat tympanogram (type B), type B/C2, or effusion observed on pneumatic otoscopy
positive_direction: Lower incidence of persistent middle ear effusion, favoring autoinflation (RR < 1)
search_queries: autoinflation otitis media with effusion children trial
nasal balloon middle ear effusion randomized controlled
inclusion_criteria: Children under 18 years of age with a diagnosis of otitis media with effusion (OME)
Randomised controlled trials evaluating autoinflation (nasal balloon, carnival blower, or commercial device) compared to watchful waiting, no treatment, or standard care
Quantitative reporting of middle ear effusion persistence or resolution/clearance within 2 to 6 weeks of follow-up
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, guidelines, and theoretical papers are excluded)
Control group receiving sham autoinflation, placebo, or an active treatment; or autoinflation administered as an add-on to other treatment in only one arm; or non-randomized designs
No quantitative data on middle ear effusion persistence or resolution at 2 to 6 weeks follow-up that can produce an effect size
Studies conducted exclusively in adults (18+ years), evaluating surgical interventions (e.g., tympanostomy tubes/grommets), or completely unrelated conditions
moderators_to_extract: autoinflation device type (commercial nasal balloon vs carnival blower vs other)
unit of analysis (per-child vs per-ear with design effect adjustment)
follow-up duration within the 2 to 6 week window (weeks)
diagnostic criteria for persistence (tympanometry type B vs type B/C2 vs pneumatic otoscopy)
effect_size_note: Pool as Risk Ratio (RR) using a random-effects model. RR < 1 indicates less persistent effusion favoring autoinflation. Convert resolution/improvement to persistence (total minus resolved). For per-ear reporting in bilateral disease, apply design effect adjustment: 1 + (average ears per child - 1) * 0.5. Prefer per-child data over per-ear data if both are available. Select follow-up closest to 4 weeks within the 2 to 6 week window (latest if multiple within window).
single_outcome_target: persistence of otitis media with effusion
